'''''Tillandsia caput-medusae''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the bromeliad family, [[Bromeliaceae]], subfamily [[Tillandsioideae]].  Common names include '''octopus plant''' and '''medusa's head'''. An [[epiphyte]] native to [[Central America]] and [[Mexico]], ''T. caput-medusae'' is a commonly cultivated bromeliad species. The thick, channeled, tapering and twisting leaves are up to {{convert|25|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and are covered in fine gray hairs. The rosette of leaves arise from an inflated [[pseudobulb]]. Pups are produced after blooming, as is usual with most ''Tillandsia'' species.

In a greenhouse, the plants can bloom from spring to early summer. The red inflorescences are usually unbranched or digitate. Bright violet flowers are about {{convert|3.2|cm|in|abbr=on}} long with the stamens exerted.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.plantoftheweek.org/week361.shtml |first=Cal |last=Lemke |title=''Tillandsia caput-medusae'' Bromeliaceae |work=Cal's Plant of the Week |date=2006-05-26 |accessdate=2011-11-01}}</ref>

''Tillandsia caput-medusae'' does not have any free water retention in its overlapping leaves because its abaxial and adaxial leaf bases provides [[Trichome|trichomes]] which coats the leaves.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Benzing|first=David H.|date=1970|title=An Investigation of Two Bromeliad Myrmecophytes: Tillandsia butzii Mez, T. caput-medusae E. Morren, and Their Ants|journal=Bulletin of the Torrey Botanical Club|volume=97|issue=2|pages=109–115|doi=10.2307/2483400|jstor=2483400|issn=0040-9618}}</ref> The significance of [[trichome]] is to enhance leaf permeability.<ref name=":0" />
